problem_type: unbounded Electron quit and window-close lifecycle drains
symptom: On macOS 0.23.0, clicking quit could leave the Electron main process alive indefinitely; a renderer that never answered close confirmation could also keep a window from closing forever.
direct_cause: Multiple modules independently prevented will-quit and waited on promises without a shared deadline; windowCloseConfirmation prevented every repeated close while waiting for an unbounded renderer response; Windows session end, the dev parent watchdog, and MCP stdio shutdown ended the process with app.exit and skipped every drain. Round 6 (independent acceptance V-1125, real Windows Electron): after a successful drain the owner called app.quit() again to finish; the drains settle inside the microtask checkpoint of the will-quit dispatch it prevented, where Electron is still quitting and ignores app.quit(), so the windowless process never exited. origin/main had the same swallowed call hidden behind a 3s force-exit timer (every normal quit took ~3.2s and logged a false quit-timeout).
class_root: Process termination had no single owner: any module could subscribe to the quit lifecycle or end the process directly, so no path was guaranteed to run the drains under one deadline. The owner itself must end the process with exactly one terminal call (app.exit) and one deadline timer; re-entering Electron's quit state machine from inside its own dispatch is unreliable, and fakes that model app.quit as an independent recorder cannot see it.
affected_population: macOS users quitting while local task or Antigravity work is active
users whose renderer is stalled or disconnected during close confirmation
Windows users who shut down, restart, or log off with Nomi open (exports and Agent lane were never drained)
MCP stdio hosts and dev/e2e launchers whose child Nomi process ended without draining
entry_points: Electron before-quit and will-quit lifecycle (Cmd+Q, Dock quit, app.quit, last window on Windows/Linux, electron-updater quitAndInstall)
Windows BrowserWindow query-session-end / session-end and Linux powerMonitor shutdown
MCP stdio transport close and MCP stdio startup failure
video depth, screenshot, watchdog, and catalog lifecycle cleanup
external_sources: node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts (Electron 43.4.1) App 'before-quit': On Windows, this event will not be emitted if the app is closed due to a shutdown/restart of the system or a user logout.
node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts (Electron 43.4.1) App.exit: before-quit and will-quit events will not be emitted.
node_modules/electron-updater (6.8.9) out/BaseUpdater.js quitAndInstall: spawns the installer, then this.app.quit(); out/MacUpdater.js hands off to Squirrel nativeUpdater.quitAndInstall.
Real Electron 43.4.1 probe (Windows, off-screen): app.quit() called during the will-quit task produced no further before-quit / will-quit / quit events; deferring it by one macrotask exited in 247ms.

node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts (Electron 43.4.1) powerMonitor 'shutdown': docs say e.preventDefault() delays shutdown while the listener is typed () => void; Electron's bundled lib/browser/api/power-monitor.ts takes the logind delay lock via setListeningForShutdown and assigns the native emit to the JS emitter, which passes the event object first.
internal_only_reason: Electron supplies the events; which drains run, in what order, under which deadline, and who may end the process is an application-owned contract.
invariants: Only electron/quitTeardown.ts subscribes to before-quit, will-quit, BrowserWindow query-session-end/session-end, or powerMonitor shutdown (ESLint no-restricted-syntax, any of on/once/addListener/prependListener/prependOnceListener).

Only electron/quitTeardown.ts calls app.exit or app.relaunch in the GUI process; two reviewed file exemptions remain: capabilityCore/host.ts (separate one-shot Electron entry where the owner is never installed) and update/autoUpdater.ts (quitAndInstall ends in app.quit and re-enters the owner).

The normal quit budget starts at will-quit; built-ins run serially background-lifecycle -> capability-core -> active-exports (250ms cap each) -> desktop-lane-ipc (all remaining budget), then registered required drains; a step timeout is logged with its step name and the next step still runs; at the total deadline the owner calls app.exit.
Unattended exits (Windows session end, Linux shutdown, lost dev launcher) run only active-exports then desktop-lane-ipc within 500ms, never show a confirmation, and then app.exit(0).

Close confirmation never discards unsaved content without an explicit user choice: renderer ACK within 1500ms hands the decision to the user with no timeout; no ACK shows one native Force Quit / Cancel dialog (default Cancel); a confirmed close resumes the quit it interrupted.

The owner ends the GUI process only through app.exit, from one finish() guarded by teardownFinished, and one owner deadline timer that an unattended exit re-arms (never extends); a drain already running cannot hold the process past the shortened deadline, and drains not yet started that are not critical are skipped.
A renderer that ACKed a close and then crashed (render-process-gone) or hung (unresponsive) is treated like a missing ACK: the native Force Quit / Cancel dialog decides.

door_reduction.why_not: Before: seven lifecycle subscriptions, four direct app.exit calls (main.ts MCP failure, mcpStdioServer close, parent watchdog, host.ts) and the updater restart; Windows session end had no door at all. After: one owner (installQuitTeardown) holds every subscription and every GUI-process exit; eleven doors are calls into it (six registrations, two quit requests, one unattended exit, close-cancel reset, close-confirmed resume), and two are reviewed exemptions outside the GUI owner path (host.ts separate process, autoUpdater.quitAndInstall that re-enters the owner through app.quit). Each call-in door is a distinct caller intent; merging them would push caller knowledge back into the owner.

generality_proof: Every way to end the GUI process is either an Electron lifecycle event the owner alone subscribes to, or an owner function (requestQuit, exitWithoutConfirmation). ESLint rejects new subscriptions to quit or session-end events and new app.exit/app.relaunch/autoUpdater.quitAndInstall calls anywhere in electron/ except the owner and two named exemption files, so a new module cannot add a second termination path without editing eslint.config.mjs in review.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own before-quit/will-quit and platform session-end subscriptions, ordered drains, per-step and total deadlines, and the final app.quit/app.exit.
Require every cleanup participant to declare required/optional and its deadline before the owner runs it.
Single unattended exit: 500ms critical drains, then app.exit(0).
Normal quit request from code, with optional process exit code, routed through will-quit drains.
Renderer ACK liveness, user decision without timeout, native fallback dialog, and quit resume after a confirmed close.
Reject production quit/session-end subscriptions and direct exit/relaunch/updater calls outside the owner or the two exemptions.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Image job cancelAll is an owner drain; taskIpcHandlers.test.ts drives the real owner: one cancelAll across repeated will-quit, quit only after cleanup settles.
Cancel and settlement are an owner drain; antigravityIpc.test.ts drives the real owner: single cancel, refuses new tests after before-quit, waits for persistence before quit.
ACK / decision / native dialog / quit resume covered by windowCloseConfirmation.test.ts against the real owner.
Video job disposal is an owner drain rather than a direct will-quit listener.
Parent watchdog exit calls exitWithoutConfirmation; mainProcessLifecycle.test.ts asserts exports abort and lane close before app.exit.
Transport close calls requestQuit() instead of app.exit(0).
Calls requestQuit({ exitCode: 1 }); owner exits with code 1 after drains (quitTeardown.test.ts).
Separate one-shot Electron entry with no spawner today (see mcpResultEnrichLive.ts note); main.ts and the owner never load there. ESLint file exemption with reason comment.
electron-updater quitAndInstall ends in app.quit (BaseUpdater) or Squirrel's quit (MacUpdater), re-entering the owner. ESLint file exemption with reason comment.

recurrence.reason: Any new asynchronous cleanup, platform exit event, or direct process exit could recreate an undrained or unbounded termination path unless subscription and exit ownership are structural.
same_class_scan: node scripts/door-map.mjs registerQuitDrain: six registration files.
node scripts/door-map.mjs requestQuit / exitWithoutConfirmation / continueRequestedQuit / resetQuitRequest: listed in doors.
git grep for app.exit/app.relaunch/quitAndInstall in electron/ (excluding tests and fixtures): only quitTeardown.ts, capabilityCore/host.ts, update/autoUpdater.ts remain.
git grep for on/once/addListener of before-quit, will-quit, query-session-end, session-end, shutdown in electron/ and src/: only quitTeardown.ts.

prevention.invariant: All termination goes through the owner; drains run serially under one deadline started at will-quit (3000ms) or at the unattended-exit trigger (500ms).
prevention.failure_mode: A thrown drain is logged as <step>-failed and the next step runs; a step timeout is logged as <step>-timeout and the next step runs; every step leaves a quit-step receipt and every exit one quit-exit receipt (reason completed / step-timeout / deadline / <unattended reason>); the only terminal call is app.exit.
prevention.strategy: Delete per-module lifecycle listeners and direct exits, route every remaining caller through owner functions, and make ESLint reject new subscriptions and direct exits. Not exceptions to the GUI-process invariant: capabilityCore/host.ts is a separate process where the owner never exists, and autoUpdater.quitAndInstall ends in app.quit, which re-enters the owner; both are named in eslint.config.mjs directQuitExemptionFiles with reason comments. ESLint keys the lifecycle ban on the event names themselves (any Literal / template element spelling will-quit, before-quit, query-session-end, session-end, or a call argument shutdown), so aliases, computed keys and bind cannot hide a subscription; app.exit / app.relaunch are banned in every access form (alias, destructure, computed, optional chain, electron.app.exit) in files that take app from electron, and aliasing app is banned.

legacy_paths.rationale: Per-module quit listeners and direct app.exit calls were deleted in the same change; no fallback listener or exit remains.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency upgrade controls this application-owned lifecycle invariant.

migration: No persisted data or external protocol changes; existing runtime registrations converge on the new owner during process startup.
residual_risks: Windows query-session-end preventDefault and 500ms drain timing are unit-verified only; not run on a real Windows shutdown/logoff.

Resume-after-confirmed-close relies on reading Electron's Browser::OnWindowCloseCancelled (a prevented window close cancels an in-flight quit); not verified on a packaged macOS build. The resume is idempotent if Electron did not cancel.
Windows/Linux session end exits without asking the renderer to save; unsaved renderer edits since the last autosave can be lost. Open product decision recorded in the PR body.
Owner total timeout stays 3000ms by default; revisit only with measured lifecycle evidence.
Linux powerMonitor shutdown preventDefault relies on Electron docs and its bundled JS wiring (typings disagree); not run on a real Linux shutdown.

electron-updater quitAndInstall is covered at the owner level (windows closed before before-quit still drains and exits once) and by the ordinary confirm-then-resume path; not run against a real installer.

tests/ux/quit-teardown-real.e2e.mjs has no CI runner yet (architecture review row 5: 40 explicit *.e2e.mjs files are unwired; owned by the lifecycle e2e wiring line). Real Windows run is in this PR's evidence; Linux/macOS real runs are unverified.
